literal: The day after Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Ye city, Jingxian was seized and executed outside the Changhe Gate, blamed for not remaining at Jinyang.
idiomatic: The day after Emperor Wu of Zhou took Ye, Jingxian was seized and beheaded outside the Changhe Gate — punished for failing to hold Jinyang.

literal: Gao Shigui was a native of Shanwu.
idiomatic: Gao Shigui was a man of Shanwu.

literal: From youth he had martial ability.
idiomatic: From youth he had a soldier's gift.

literal: At the beginning of Xiaochang, Liu Lun and others of the Chile tribe within Heng Province gathered crowds in rebellion; Shigui served as commander, led troops to attack Lun, and defeated him in one battle.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiaochang, Liu Lun and other Chile tribesmen within Heng Province rose in rebellion. Shigui served as commander, led troops against Lun, and broke him in a single battle.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army and Remonstrance Advisor.
idiomatic: He rose by stages to general who pacifies the army and remonstrance advisor.

literal: When Erzhu Rong enthroned Emperor Zhuang of Wei, Shigui shared in the merit of supporting the throne; he was transferred to Guard General, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Commander of Xiurong, First Chieftain of Registered Tribal Peoples, and enfeoffed Baron of Shangluo County.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong enthroned Emperor Zhuang of Wei, Shigui shared in the merit of raising him up and was made guard general, grand master of splendid happiness, grand commander of Xiurong, first chieftain of registered tribal peoples, and baron of Shangluo County.

literal: When Erzhu Rong attacked Ge Rong at Fukou, Shigui was made vanguard commander.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong struck Ge Rong at Fukou, Shigui was made vanguard commander.

literal: When Rong was pacified, he was appointed Commissioner with Full Powers and Governor of Fen Province; soon he became Governor of Jin Province.
idiomatic: After Rong was pacified, he was appointed commissioner with full powers and governor of Fen Province; soon he became governor of Jin Province.

literal: When Heduoling Bufan invaded and harassed Bing Province, the Grand Ancestor defeated him; Shigui also followed on campaign with merit and was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Senior Grand Master of Equal Rank with the Three Dukes, enfeoffed Duke of Changshan Commandery with a fief of one thousand five hundred households.
idiomatic: When Heduoling Bufan raided Bing Province, Gao Huan broke him; Shigui followed on campaign with merit and was made grand general of agile cavalry, senior grand master equal in rank to the three dukes, and duke of Changshan Commandery with a fief of fifteen hundred households.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor raised the standard of revolt, Shigui took part in the planning.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised the standard of revolt, Shigui took part in the planning.

literal: When Fan Ziguo seized the province in rebellion, he followed Grand Commander Lou Zhao to suppress him.
idiomatic: When Fan Ziguo seized the province in rebellion, he followed Grand Commander Lou Zhao to put him down.

literal: When Ziguo was pacified, he was made Governor of Western Yan Province but did not go to the province.
idiomatic: When Ziguo was pacified, he was made governor of Western Yan Province but never took up the post.

literal: At the beginning of Tianping, he was again appointed Governor of Jin Province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianping he was again appointed governor of Jin Province.

literal: The Grand Ancestor soon, because Hongdong was strategically crucial, dispatched Shigui to guard it.
idiomatic: Gao Huan soon sent Shigui to hold Hongdong, a place of critical terrain.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor suffered defeat at Shaya, the acting governor of Jin Province Feng Zuye abandoned the city and fled back; provincial resident Chai Lan gathered crowds in rebellion.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan lost at Shaya, Feng Zuye, acting governor of Jin Province, abandoned the city and fled; the provincial man Chai Lan gathered a crowd and rose in revolt.

literal: The Grand Ancestor ordered Shigui to attack Lan; Lan fled to Chai Fortress; Shigui defeated and killed him.
idiomatic: Gao Huan ordered Shigui against Lan. Lan fled to Chai Fortress; Shigui broke him there and cut off his head.

literal: At that time the territory of Eastern Yong and Southern Fen provinces had many bandit groups gathering as robbers; because Shigui pacified Lan, they all dispersed and returned to their occupations.
idiomatic: At that time Eastern Yong and Southern Fen were thick with bandits who had gathered into robber bands; once Shigui pacified Lan, they scattered and returned to their fields.

literal: Later five thousand households of Xiurong rebelled in response to the Shanhu; Shigui was again made Mobile Office commander, commanding various armies to suppress and pacify them.
idiomatic: Later five thousand Xiurong households rebelled in answer to the Shanhu. Shigui was again made mobile-office commander and led the armies that suppressed them.

literal: In the Yuanxiang era, he followed the Grand Ancestor in defeating Emperor Wen of Zhou at Mount Mang.
idiomatic: In the Yuanxiang era he followed Gao Huan in defeating Emperor Wen of Zhou at Mount Mang.

literal: He was again appointed Governor of Jin Province and Western Circuit Army Marshal, leading troops to attack the rebel Pan Ji of Huai Province.
idiomatic: He was again made governor of Jin Province and western-circuit army marshal, leading troops against the Huai Province rebel Pan Ji.

literal: Before he arrived, he fell ill and died on the road.
idiomatic: Before he arrived he fell ill and died on the road.

literal: Posthumously granted Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs for the five provinces of Bing, Fen, Huai, Jian, and Eastern Yong, Duke Grand Commandant, Governor of Bing Province.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted commander-in-chief of military affairs for Bing, Fen, Huai, Jian, and Eastern Yong, duke grand commandant, and governor of Bing Province.

literal: His son Kenazhu enjoyed high favor and was enfeoffed Prince of Chenggao.
idiomatic: His son Kenazhu rose in high favor and was enfeoffed Prince of Chenggao.

literal: An edict ordered his second son Kongque to inherit the title.
idiomatic: An edict ordered his second son Kongque to inherit the title.

literal: Kudi Huiluo was a native of Dai.
idiomatic: Kudi Huiluo was a man of Dai.

literal: From youth he had martial strength; his bearing and appearance were imposing.
idiomatic: From youth he had martial strength, and his bearing and frame were imposing.

literal: At first he served Erzhu Rong as army commander, took part in enthroning Emperor Zhuang, was transferred to separate commander, and enfeoffed Baron of Wuji.
idiomatic: At first he served Erzhu Rong as army commander, took part in enthroning Emperor Zhuang, was transferred to separate commander, and enfeoffed baron of Wuji.

literal: Following the defeat of Ge Rong, he was transferred to commander.
idiomatic: After Ge Rong was broken, he was transferred to commander.

literal: When Rong died, he came under Erzhu Zhao.
idiomatic: When Rong died, he passed to Erzhu Zhao.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor raised troops at Xindu, Huiluo brought his followers and submitted in loyalty.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised troops at Xindu, Huiluo brought his followers over in loyalty.

literal: Following the defeat of the Four Hus at Hanling, for military merit he was made commander, additionally Rear General and Grand Master of Palace Counsel, enfeoffed Viscount of Shunyang County with a fief of four hundred households.
idiomatic: After the Four Hus were broken at Hanling, he was made commander for military merit, additionally rear general and grand master of palace counsel, and enfeoffed viscount of Shunyang County with four hundred households.

literal: He was transferred to right-wing commander.
idiomatic: He was transferred to right-wing commander.

literal: Campaigning against the Shanhu, as vanguard he severed heads; he was appointed Governor of Shuo Province.
idiomatic: On campaign against the Shanhu he served as vanguard and took heads; he was appointed governor of Shuo Province.

literal: He defeated Zhou Wen at Heyang and was transferred and granted Governor of Xia Province.
idiomatic: He defeated Zhou Wen at Heyang and was transferred to governor of Xia Province.

literal: At the Battle of Mount Mang, he fought hard with merit; his fief was increased to seven hundred households in all with previous holdings.
idiomatic: At Mount Mang he fought hard with merit; his fief was increased to seven hundred households in all.

literal: When Shizong succeeded to affairs, he followed in pacifying Yingchuan.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng succeeded to affairs, he followed in pacifying Yingchuan.

literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, he was appointed Governor of Jian Province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he was appointed governor of Jian Province.

literal: When Emperor Suzong took the throne, he was enfeoffed Prince of Shunyang Commandery.
idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong took the throne, he was enfeoffed Prince of Shunyang Commandery.

literal: At the beginning of Daning, he was transferred to Governor of Shuo Province, drawing income from Boling Commandery dry rations.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Daning he was transferred to governor of Shuo Province, drawing income from Boling Commandery dry rations.

literal: He was transferred to Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince; he fell ill and died.
idiomatic: He was transferred to grand tutor of the crown prince, fell ill, and died.

literal: Posthumously granted Commissioner with Full Powers, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs for the five provinces of Ding, Ying, Heng, Shuo, and Yun, Grand General, Duke Grand Commandant, Governor of Ding Province, with one thousand rolls of gifts.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted commissioner with full powers, commander-in-chief of military affairs for Ding, Ying, Heng, Shuo, and Yun, grand general, duke grand commandant, and governor of Ding Province, with one thousand rolls of gifts.

literal: Kudi Sheng was a native of Huaishuo.
idiomatic: Kudi Sheng was a man of Huaishuo.

literal: His nature was gentle and yielding; from youth he had martial ability.
idiomatic: His nature was gentle and yielding, yet from youth he had martial ability.

literal: At first he was the Grand Ancestor's trusted personal commander, appointed General Who Quells Waves, and always followed on campaigns.
idiomatic: At first he was Gao Huan's trusted personal commander, appointed general who quells waves, and always followed on campaign.

literal: For merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Xingtang County, repeatedly promoted to General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of You Province, additionally made Central Army General and fortress garrison commander of Yu Province.
idiomatic: For merit he was enfeoffed baron of Xingtang County, then repeatedly promoted to general who pacifies the north and governor of You Province, additionally made central army general and fortress garrison commander of Yu Province.

literal: As an old merit-holder he was advanced to duke; Shizong reduced the fief by two hundred households to increase his fief.
idiomatic: As an old merit-holder he was advanced to duke; Gao Cheng reduced other fiefs by two hundred households to augment his.

literal: He was appointed Grand General Who Conquers the West, Senior Grand Master of State with Full Powers Equal to the Three Dukes, and Governor of Shuo Province.
idiomatic: He was appointed grand general who conquers the west, senior grand master of state with full powers equal to the three dukes, and governor of Shuo Province.

literal: When Qi received the abdication, his title was changed to Duke of Huayang County.
idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, his title was changed to duke of Huayang County.

literal: He was again appointed Governor of Northern Shuo Province; because his Huayang fief was far away, by precedent portions were cut from Shi'ai County of Bing Province, Pingkou County of Si Province, and Mayi County of Yuanping, several tens of households each, totaling two hundred households as his food fief.
idiomatic: He was again appointed governor of Northern Shuo Province. Because his Huayang fief lay far away, by precedent several tens of households each were cut from Shi'ai County in Bing Province, Pingkou County in Si Province, and Mayi County in Yuanping — two hundred households in all — as his food fief.

literal: Before long, by precedent dismissed, he was appointed Special Advancement and died.
idiomatic: Before long, by precedent dismissed from provincial office, he was appointed special advancement and died.

literal: Posthumously granted Commissioner with Full Powers, Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs for the five provinces of Shuo, Ying, Zhao, You, and An, Duke Grand Commandant, Governor of Shuo Province.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted commissioner with full powers, commander-in-chief of military affairs for Shuo, Ying, Zhao, You, and An, duke grand commandant, and governor of Shuo Province.

literal: Xue Guyan was a native of Dai.
idiomatic: Xue Guyan was a man of Dai.

literal: From youth he was bold and resolute, with martial strength.
idiomatic: From youth he was bold and resolute, with a soldier's strength.

literal: When Han Lou rebelled, Yan followed the crowd and submitted to him.
idiomatic: When Han Lou rebelled, Guyan followed the crowd and submitted to him.

literal: Later he secretly plotted with Wang Huai and others to attack Lou; Lou's commandery captain Yifu Chou detected it; they fought hard and defeated Chou, then together led their followers back.
idiomatic: Later he secretly plotted with Wang Huai and others to attack Lou. Lou's commandery captain Yifu Chou discovered it; they fought hard, broke Chou, and together led their followers back.

literal: Mobile Office Liu Gui memorialized to make him commander, additionally General Who Captures Barbarians, enfeoffed Marquis of Yonggu County.
idiomatic: Mobile-office Liu Gui memorialized to make him commander, additionally general who captures barbarians, and enfeoffed him marquis of Yonggu County.

literal: Later he came under the Grand Ancestor as commander and still followed in raising the revolt.
idiomatic: Later he came under Gao Huan as commander and still followed in raising the revolt.

literal: He defeated Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a, followed in pacifying Ye; for merit he was advanced to duke and transferred to grand commander.
idiomatic: He defeated Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a and followed in pacifying Ye; for merit he was advanced to duke and transferred to grand commander.

literal: He followed in defeating the Four Hus at Hanling and was made Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle.
idiomatic: He followed in defeating the Four Hus at Hanling and was made grand master of the golden seal and purple girdle.

literal: He followed in pursuing Erzhu Zhao at Chihong Ridge and was appointed First Chieftain of Registered Tribal Peoples.
idiomatic: He followed in pursuing Erzhu Zhao at Chihong Ridge and was appointed first chieftain of registered tribal peoples.

literal: When Emperor Xiaojing was enthroned, he was appointed Governor of Xian Province and repeatedly promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaojing was enthroned, he was appointed governor of Xian Province and repeatedly promoted to general of chariots and cavalry.

literal: In the fourth year of Tianping, he followed the Grand Ancestor on the western campaign.
idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianping he followed Gao Huan on the western campaign.

literal: Reaching Pujin, Dou Tai suffered defeat south of the river at Henan; the Grand Ancestor withdrew; Yan served as rearguard, fighting as they went; in one day he broke fifteen sword blades.
idiomatic: At Pujin, Dou Tai was defeated south of the river in Henan; Gao Huan withdrew. Guyan served as rearguard, fighting as he went — in one day he broke fifteen sword blades.

literal: On return, he was transferred to Governor of Liang Province.
idiomatic: On his return he was transferred to governor of Liang Province.

literal: Following the campaign against Yubi, he was again transferred to Governor of Heng Province.
idiomatic: Following the campaign against Yubi, he was again transferred to governor of Heng Province.

literal: He followed in defeating Emperor Wen of Zhou at Mount Mang, was advanced to commandery duke with a fief of one thousand households.
idiomatic: He followed in defeating Emperor Wen of Zhou at Mount Mang and was advanced to commandery duke with a fief of one thousand households.

literal: The Grand Ancestor once inspected horses at the northern pasture; on the road they encountered torrential rain, great thunder shaking the earth.
idiomatic: Gao Huan once inspected horses at the northern pasture. On the road they met torrential rain and thunder that shook the earth.

literal: Ahead was a pagoda; the Grand Ancestor ordered Yan to go inspect it.
idiomatic: Ahead stood a pagoda; Gao Huan ordered Guyan to go inspect it.

literal: Yan galloped forward spear in hand; before reaching thirty paces, lightning fire burned his face; Yan shouted and charged, circled the pagoda running, and the fire then extinguished.
idiomatic: Guyan galloped forward spear in hand. Before he had gone thirty paces, lightning fire burned his face; he shouted and charged, circled the pagoda at a run, and the fire went out.

literal: When Yan returned, eyebrows, sideburns, and the horse's mane and tail were all singed.
idiomatic: When Guyan returned, his brows, sideburns, and the horse's mane and tail were all singed.

literal: The Grand Ancestor sighed: "Xue Guyan can actually fight with thunderbolts!
idiomatic: Gao Huan sighed: "Xue Guyan can actually fight thunderbolts!

literal: " Such was his valor and resolution.
idiomatic: " Such was his valor and resolution.

literal: He also repeatedly followed the Grand Ancestor in defeating the Shanhu and attacking Yubi in the west.
idiomatic: He also repeatedly followed Gao Huan in defeating the Shanhu and attacking Yubi in the west.

literal: He entered court as Left Guard General; his title was changed to Duke of Pingqin Commandery.
idiomatic: He entered court as left guard general and was re-enfeoffed duke of Pingqin Commandery.

literal: He served as Grand Commander of the Left Wing, with various generals attacking Ying Province.
idiomatic: He served as grand commander of the left wing, with the other generals attacking Ying Province.

literal: Yan was solely supervising construction of the earthen siege mound; being drunk on wine, the enemy seized it in a raid.
idiomatic: Guyan was solely supervising construction of the earthen siege mound; drunk on wine, he let the enemy seize it in a raid.

literal: When Ying Province was pacified, the generals returned to the capital and feasted in Hualin Park.
idiomatic: When Ying Province was pacified, the generals returned to the capital and feasted in Hualin Park.

literal: Shizong reported to the Wei Emperor and had Yan seated on the steps below to humiliate him.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng reported to the Wei emperor and had Guyan seated on the steps below to humiliate him.

literal: Later he additionally held the post of General Who Leads the Army, went out as Governor of Cang Province, and was separately enfeoffed Baron of Wen County with a fief of three hundred households.
idiomatic: Later he additionally held the post of general who leads the army, went out as governor of Cang Province, and was separately enfeoffed baron of Wen County with three hundred households.

literal: When Qi received the abdication, he was separately granted title Duke of Duchang County.
idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, he was separately granted the title duke of Duchang County.

literal: His nature loved wine; mostly he was drunk and muddled.
idiomatic: He loved wine by nature and was most often drunk and muddled.

literal: Yet because of his valor, resolution, and skill in battle, whenever the great army marched on campaign he was always vanguard — thus ranked with Peng, Liu, Han, and Pan.
idiomatic: Yet for his valor, resolution, and skill in battle, whenever the great army marched he was always vanguard — and so ranked with Peng, Liu, Han, and Pan.

literal: In the second year of Tianbao, he was made Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince and transferred to Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
idiomatic: In the second year of Tianbao he was made grand mentor of the crown prince, then transferred to grand tutor of the crown prince.

literal: In the eighth year, he was appointed Governor of Si Province, additionally Senior Grand Master of State with Full Powers Equal to the Three Dukes, drawing income from Luoyang Commandery dry rations; soon changed to draw from Hejian Commandery dry rations.
idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed governor of Si Province, additionally senior grand master of state with full powers equal to the three dukes, drawing income from Luoyang Commandery dry rations; soon changed to Hejian Commandery dry rations.

literal: Zhang Baoluo was a native of Dai; he claimed his origin was Xie of Nanyang.
idiomatic: Zhang Baoluo was a man of Dai; he claimed descent from Xie in Nanyang.

literal: His family for generations loved hosting guests, valued chivalry and bold spirit, and was frequently known among the northern lands.
idiomatic: His family for generations loved guests, honored bold spirit, and was well known across the northern lands.

literal: Baoluo from youth was forthright and robust, skilled in bow and horse.
idiomatic: Baoluo from youth was forthright and robust, skilled with bow and horse.

literal: In the Xiaochang era of Wei, when the northern garrisons were in turmoil, Baoluo also followed the masses south.
idiomatic: In the Xiaochang era of Wei, when the northern garrisons fell into turmoil, Baoluo followed the crowds south.

literal: Ge Rong usurped; he made Baoluo leader of the left and right guard.
idiomatic: Ge Rong usurped power and made Baoluo leader of the left and right guard.

literal: When Rong was defeated, he still served Erzhu Rong as army commander and was repeatedly promoted to General Who Raises the Array and Chief Commandant Who Attends the Chariot.
idiomatic: When Rong was defeated, he still served Erzhu Rong as army commander and rose to general who raises the array and chief commandant who attends the chariot.

literal: Later he came under the Grand Ancestor as commander, following to attack Bufan.
idiomatic: Later he came under Gao Huan as commander and followed to attack Bufan.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor raised the revolt, Baoluo served in the personal guard, following to defeat Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised the revolt, Baoluo served in the personal guard and followed to defeat Erzhu Zhao at Guang'a.

literal: Soon he was transferred to Right General and Palace Attendant Forbearing Counsel, still in the personal guard following the Grand Ancestor in besieging Ye; once it was taken, he was made General Who Pacifies the South and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to right general and palace attendant forbearing counsel, still in the personal guard following Gao Huan in besieging Ye; once the city fell, he was made general who pacifies the south and grand master of splendid happiness.

literal: He followed in defeating Erzhu Zhao and others at Hanling, then followed the Grand Ancestor into Luoyang, additionally made General Who Pacifies the East.
idiomatic: He followed in defeating Erzhu Zhao and others at Hanling, then followed Gao Huan into Luoyang and was additionally made general who pacifies the east.

literal: Later the Grand Ancestor proposed reducing state fiefs and distributing them to officers and soldiers; Baoluo by precedent was enfeoffed Baron of Bojia City Township, Changping County, with one hundred households.
idiomatic: Later Gao Huan proposed reducing state fiefs and distributing them among officers and soldiers; Baoluo by precedent was enfeoffed baron of Bojia City Township in Changping County with one hundred households.

literal: Emperor Chu of Wei was at odds with the Grand Ancestor; he ordered Senior Grand Master of Equal Rank Jia Xianzhi to lead Yu Province Governor Husishou east toward Ji Province.
idiomatic: Emperor Chu of Wei was at odds with Gao Huan; he ordered senior grand master of equal rank Jia Xianzhi to lead Yu Province governor Husishou east toward Ji Province.

literal: The Grand Ancestor dispatched Grand Commander Dou Tai to cross the river from Huatai to resist Xianzhi; Baoluo served under Tai as vanguard.
idiomatic: Gao Huan dispatched Grand Commander Dou Tai to cross from Huatai and resist Xianzhi; Baoluo served under Tai as vanguard.

literal: When the affair was settled, he was transferred to commander.
idiomatic: When the affair was settled, he was transferred to commander.

literal: He followed the Grand Ancestor in raiding Xia Province and captured it.
idiomatic: He followed Gao Huan in raiding Xia Province and took it.

literal: When Wan Qishouluogan surrendered, the Grand Ancestor dispatched Baoluo with various generals to receive and support him on the road.
idiomatic: When Wan Qishouluogan surrendered, Gao Huan dispatched Baoluo with the other generals to receive and support him on the road.
